title: Phase-Sensitive Benchmarking of Composite Quantum Gates with Chiral-Interference Circuits on Quantum Hardware
authors: Georgi M. Aleksandrov, Nikolay V. Vitanov
abstract: We construct and experimentally implement compact gate-native circuits that simulate the state-transfer interference underlying three- and four-level chiral-resolution protocols. Both models are encoded in a two-qubit register, with the enantiomer-dependent sign of one of the couplings simulated by a conditional-phase operation in the four-level circuit and by the sign of a final rotation in the three-level circuit. On an IBM quantum processor, the two circuits produce the expected enantiomer-dependent output states with probabilities of nearly $98\%$. We then use these circuits as physically motivated, phase-sensitive benchmarks for composite quantum gates. We introduce rotation-angle error to the single-qubit operations and replace them by several composite gates, including B5, SK1, BB1, H5s, and X5. The comparison demonstrates that single-gate robustness does not translate to equivalent whole-circuit robustness. In particular, variable-rotation sequences do not preserve the required relative phases, making them unsuitable for error correction in circuits. By contrast, the H5s/X5 sequences maintain high target-state populations for relative errors as large as $50\%$, whereas elementary rotations reach the same threshold only for approximately $8\%$. The three-level circuit exhibits a similar enhancement and additionally reveals an error-cancellation symmetry whose protection under composite replacement is exact only when the relevant full propagators satisfy an inverse relation.
summary: The paper experimentally benchmarks composite quantum gates using chiral-interference circuits to test error resilience. By introducing systematic rotation errors, the authors demonstrate that single-gate performance does not guarantee overall circuit robustness. They show that specific constant composite sequences maintain coherence far better than variable ones when facing correlated noise.
main_problem: The study benchmarks composite quantum gates by using phase-sensitive circuits that simulate chiral-interference protocols to test if single-gate robustness guarantees whole-circuit robustness.
main_result: Single-gate robustness does not translate to equivalent whole-circuit robustness, as variable-rotation sequences fail to preserve required relative phases for error correction. Constant composite rotations (H5s/X5) showed significantly higher resilience to systematic errors than elementary rotations.
method: The authors implemented two gate-native circuits (three- and four-level) on an IBM quantum processor, systematically introducing rotation-angle errors ($\epsilon$) into single-qubit operations for comparison.
model_or_system: The models simulate chiral state transfer using two qubits. The four-level circuit uses a conditional phase gate, while the three-level circuit models enantioselective population transfer. The benchmarking compares variable vs. constant composite rotation sequences.
key_observables: Enantiomer-dependent output state populations (achieving $\approx 98\%$ fidelity), and the maintenance of high target-state populations under varying relative errors ($\epsilon$).
important_parameters: Relative error magnitude (up to $50\%$), rotation angle error ($\epsilon$), and the specific gate sequences tested (B5, SK1, H5s, X5).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that CZ and iSWAP gates are perfect; the comparison isolates correlated coherent errors in single-qubit operations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the interferometric schemes for both four-level and three-level models, showing ideal population evolution diagrams corresponding to reduced quantum circuits.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the chiral-interference protocols (four- and three-level) as benchmarks. It then systematically compares the performance of various composite gate sequences under controlled rotation-angle errors, culminating in a detailed analysis comparing error scaling across different circuit types.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the gap between local gate fidelity and global circuit robustness, which is crucial for designing fault-tolerant quantum algorithms that rely on complex interferometry or state preparation protocols.

FIG. 3. Target-state populations of the (a) S and (b) R circuits of the four-level circuit as functions of the correlated rotation- angle error ε. Elementary rotations are compared with H5s/X5, B5 variable rotations, SK1, and BB1. The points are hardware data from ibm kingston; the solid lines are scaled theoretical predictions and the shaded bands represent twice the shot-noise uncertainty.

FIG. 4. Target-state populations of the (a) S and (b) R branches of the three-level circuit as functions of the correlated rotation-angle error ε. The target states are |01⟩and |00⟩, respectively. Elementary pulses are compared with H5s, variable rotation, SK1 and BB1 composite π/2 rotations. For the R enantiomer, elementary pulses exhibit exact cancellation of the common rotation-angle error. For composite replacements, this protection persists only when the final erroneous composite propagator is the exact inverse of the transported first propagator; asymmetric sequences can break this condition.
